texts.text: ABSTRACT

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Background: Acute appendicitis is a common surgical emergency, with appendectomy being the standard treatment. The choice between laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) and open appendectomy (OA) remains a topic of debate, particularly in resource-limited settings like Yemen.
texts.text: Background: Acute appendicitis is a common surgical emergency, with appendectomy being the standard treatment. The choice between laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) and open appendectomy (OA) remains a topic of debate, particularly in resource-limited settings like Yemen.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Aim: To compare the prevalence and descriptive patterns and crude associations of laparoscopic versus OA among insured patients in Yemen from 2022 to 2024.
texts.text: Aim: To compare the prevalence and descriptive patterns and crude associations of laparoscopic versus OA among insured patients in Yemen from 2022 to 2024.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Methods: A retrospective comparative study was conducted using data from 243 patients who underwent appendectomy (either LA or OA) at more than 40 hospitals in Yemen. Data was extracted from the medical records of patients with health insurance at Medical Insurance Specialist Company. The study compared demographic characteristics, hospital stay duration, cost, and factors influencing the choice of surgical approach.
texts.text: Methods: A retrospective comparative study was conducted using data from 243 patients who underwent appendectomy (either LA or OA) at more than 40 hospitals in Yemen. Data was extracted from the medical records of patients with health insurance at Medical Insurance Specialist Company. The study compared demographic characteristics, hospital stay duration, cost, and factors influencing the choice of surgical approach.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Results: The prevalence of OA (60.5%) was significantly higher than that of LA (39.5%). Patients undergoing OA were more likely to present with complicated appendicitis (90.9% vs. 9.1% for LA, P <0.001). Residents of Sana'a City were more likely to undergo OA compared to those from other regions (COR = 8.306, 95% CI: 2.861-24.115, P <0.001). LA was associated with higher costs (median cost: 179900 YR) compared to OA (median cost: 135000 YR; P <0.001). However, there was no significant difference in hospital stay duration between LA and OA ( P =0.676). The majority of patients (81.9%) presented with uncomplicated appendicitis, and 50.6% were discharged within one day.
texts.text: Results: The prevalence of OA (60.5%) was significantly higher than that of LA (39.5%). Patients undergoing OA were more likely to present with complicated appendicitis (90.9% vs. 9.1% for LA, P <0.001). Residents of Sana'a City were more likely to undergo OA compared to those from other regions (COR = 8.306, 95% CI: 2.861-24.115, P <0.001). LA was associated with higher costs (median cost: 179900 YR) compared to OA (median cost: 135000 YR; P <0.001). However, there was no significant difference in hospital stay duration between LA and OA ( P =0.676). The majority of patients (81.9%) presented with uncomplicated appendicitis, and 50.6% were discharged within one day.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Conclusions: OA remains the predominant surgical approach in Yemen, particularly for complex cases and in urban areas such as Sana'a.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Acute appendicitis is one of the most common causes of acute abdomen. Acute appendicitis is relatively rare in infants,  and  becomes  increasingly  common  in  childhood and early adult life, reaching a peak incidence in the teens and early 20s. The incidence of appendicitis is equal among males and females before puberty [1,2] .

texts.orig: Laparoscopic appendectomy (LA) has become a widely accepted method for diagnosing and treating acute appendicitis,  offering  advantages  such  as  better  wound healing,  reduced  postoperative  pain,  quicker  return  to diet,  earlier  hospital  discharge,  and  improved  cosmetic outcomes [6,7] .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The choice between LA and open appendectomy (OA) is influenced by the risks and benefits of each procedure, including infection rates, postoperative pain, and recovery time. The average incision size for OA is 3.5 cm, while for LA it is 3 cm. Pain levels, measured on a 1-10 scale, are  similar  between  the  two  methods,  with  both  groups reporting an average pain score of 6 [8,9] .

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This study provides real-world evidence from a resource-limited  healthcare  setting,  highlighting  a  gap between current surgical practice and international recommendations.  Guidelines  from  the  World  Society of  Emergency  Surgery  and  the  Society  of  American Gastrointestinal  and  Endoscopic  Surgeons  recommend laparoscopic  appendectomy  as  the  preferred  approach for  most  uncomplicated  and  many  complicated  cases when  feasible;  however,  open  appendectomy  remains predominant in Yemen, particularly in complicated presentations, likely due to infrastructure, insurance, and resource constraints rather than clinical factors alone. These findings underscore practice-guideline discrepancies and support  the  need  for  national  guidelines,  surgical  audit systems, expanded laparoscopic training, and policy reforms to enhance equitable access to minimally invasive surgery  in  Yemen  and  similar  low-  and  middle-income countries.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Surgical Approach Selection
texts.text: Surgical Approach Selection

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The attending surgeon determined the surgical approach (laparoscopic  or  open  appendectomy)  as  part  of  routine clinical  practice  and  was  not  guided  by  a  standardized study protocol. In accordance with published guidelines, the decision was based on preoperative clinical assessment, including patient history, physical examination, laboratory findings, imaging results, and classification of appendicitis as uncomplicated or complicated. Additional factors influencing the choice included surgeon experience and  preference,  availability  of  laparoscopic  equipment, institutional resources, patient clinical stability, and insurance authorization policies. As this was a retrospective review,  the  specific  rationale  for  selecting  the  surgical approach was not consistently documented and could not be independently evaluated.

texts.orig: The higher prevalence of OA may reflect its widespread use in settings where laparoscopic equipment or specialized surgical  expertise  is  limited. texts.label: text
texts.orig: These  findings  suggest  that  the  choice  of  surgical technique,  whether  OA  or  LA,  does  not  significantly influence the length of hospital stay in this patient cohort. Given that both groups exhibited comparable proportions of short and extended hospitalization, other factors, such as postoperative complications, patient comorbidities, or  institutional  protocols,  may  play  a  more  substantial role  in  determining  recovery  time.  Further  investigation is  necessary  to  identify  the  underlying  determinants  of hospital  stay  duration  following  appendectomy.  These findings were similar to those of Fujishiro et al. [18] ,  who reported  that  there  was  no  significant  association  of  the length  of  hospital  stay  between  patients  who  underwent laparoscopic or OA.  In contrast, Khirallah et al. [19] concluded that LA should be the initial procedure of choice for most cases of uncomplicated appendicitis.

texts.orig: The data reveal a strong association between patients' residence and the type of operation they undergo. Patients residing  in  Sana'a  City  were  significantly  more  likely to  undergo  OA  than  LA,  with  a  COR  of  8.306  (95% CI:  2.861-24.115, P <0.001).  The  higher  proportion  of OA among patients from Sana'a is likely  due  to  referral patterns  and  insurance  rules  rather  than  to  geographical location.  This  indicates  that  the  odds  of  undergoing  OA were approximately 8.3 times higher among residents of Sanaa City than among those from other areas, who served as the reference group. In contrast, patients from areas other than Sanaa City demonstrated a markedly different pattern, with 90.7% undergoing OA and only 9.3% undergoing LA. This  stark  difference  is  likely  due  to  the  referral  pattern and insurance rules rather than geographical location. The statistically significant P-value (<0.001) further reinforces the  robustness  of  this  association,  suggesting  that  the observed  relationship  is  unlikely  to  be  due  to  chance. Moreover, the 95% confidence interval for the COR (2.86124.115) does not include the null value of 1, which further supports  the  strength  and  reliability  of  the  association. This  wide  range,  however,  also  indicates  variability  in the  magnitude  of  the  effect,  which  may  warrant  further investigation into potential confounding factors or underlying mechanisms driving this disparity. In contrast, Golz et al. [20] revealed that socioeconomic advantages, such as  higher  income  and  secondary  education,  are  strongly associated with lower incidence of both operations.

texts.orig: Interpretation of the observed  associations should be  cautious  due  to  potential  confounding  inherent  in  the retrospective design. Factors such as surgeon experience, hospital resources, equipment availability, insurance approval, and disease severity may have influenced both the choice of surgical approach and outcomes. The higher use  of  open  appendectomy  in  complicated  cases  likely reflects clinical selection rather than procedural superiority. Likewise, the lack of difference in hospital stay between laparoscopic and open appendectomy, which contrasts with some published studies, may be explained by institutional discharge  practices  and  resource  limitations  rather  than surgical technique alone. The identified associations do not imply causation, as the allocation of surgical approaches was non-randomized.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This study has several limitations. Referral- and accessrelated  factors,  such  as  insurance  approval  processes, hospital infrastructure, availability of laparoscopic equipment, and surgeon expertise, were not directly measured; therefore, the higher frequency of OA in Sana'a is likely attributable to referral patterns and insurance rules rather  than  geographical  location.  Additionally,  as  the study  was  limited  to  insured  patients  and  hospitals  with laparoscopic capability, the findings cannot be generalized to  uninsured  populations,  rural  communities,  or  public hospitals without laparoscopic facilities.

texts.orig: The decision-making pathways influencing the choice of surgical  approach  were  not  explicitly  captured  in this  study.  Factors  such  as  surgeon  preference,  hospital capability, patient choice, and insurance coverage policies may have confounded the observed associations between patient  characteristics  and  the  type  of  appendectomy. As these exposure-related variables were not measured, causal inferences  regarding  determinants  of  surgical  approach should be interpreted with caution.

texts.text: CONCLUSIONS

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This  study  highlights  key  differences  between  LA and  OA  among  insured  patients  in  Yemen,  mainly  in Sana'a. OA was more common (60.5%) than LA (39.5%), particularly  in  complicated  cases  (90.9%),  likely  due  to limited  laparoscopic  resources,  expertise,  and  cost.  The cohort  was  predominantly  young  (mean  28.7  yrs)  and male (60.9%), with 82.3% from Sana'a, reflecting regional healthcare disparities. No significant difference in hospital stay was observed, while LA was costlier upfront but may reduce long-term complications. Surgical choice  was strongly  associated  with  residence;  however,  the  higher prevalence of OA in Sana'a is likely due to referral patterns and insurance rules rather than geographical location.

texts.orig: يُعد التهاب الزائدة الدودية الحاد حالة جراحية طارئة شائعة، ويُعدّ استئصال الزائدة الدودية العلاج َ  الم ُ عتاد. ولا يزال الاختيار بين : المقدمة استئصال الزائدة الدودية بالمنظار واستئصال الزائدة الدودية المفتوح موضوع نقاش، خاصة في البيئات ذات الموارد المحدودة مثل اليمن. مقارنة انتشار التهاب الزائدة الدودية بالمنظار مقابل استئصال الزائدة الدودية المفتوح والعوامل الم ُ صاحبة له بين المرضى الم ُ ؤم َّن : الهدف . 2024 و 2022 عليهم في اليمن بين عامي

texts.orig: مريضًا خضعوا لاستئصال الزائدة الدودية (سواء ً  بالمنظار أو 243 أ ُ جريت دراسة م ُ قارنة تحليلية بأثر رجعي باستخدام بيانات الطرق: مستشفى في اليمن. استُخلصت البيانات من السجلات الطبية للمرضى الم ُ ؤم َّ ن عليهم صحيًا لدى شركة التأمين 40 بالمنظار) في أكثر من الطبي الم ُ تخصصة. وقارنت الدراسة الخصائص الديموغرافية، ومدة الإقامة في المستشفى، والتكلفة، والعوامل الم ُ ؤثرة في اختيار النهج الجراحي.
